clue.text: Where to see 13 being unfair

definitions.meaning: 13 is TREWS, trousers, which are worn on the legs beneath the waistband
in boxing a blow struck too low is against the rules, hence the idiom for dirty play

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a remark about tartan trousers is a low blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is TREWS, close-fitting tartan trousers traditionally worn in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are worn beneath the waist, and the boxing idiom for an illegal low punch means dishonourable.

clue.text: venerable fellow, Timothy, in the retirement zone

indicators.note: in means the short name for Timothy sits inside the venerable man's name

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was the Anglo-Saxon monk and historian

explanation.surface: An old gentleman called Timothy is spending his days in a retirement community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' looks like old age, but it is going to bed; 'zone' is a time zone, the hour for retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night happens at a set hour, the period of the day for going to sleep.

clue.text: One's seen in the midst of bliss and pride

definitions.text: One's seen in the midst of bliss and pride

indicators.note: seen in places the word for one is inside the letters that follow
the midst of a word is all of it but its first and last letters

parts.note: One's gives ONES, the possessive's apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A big cat basks contentedly among the rest of her family group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' reads as self-esteem, but the whole clue also pictures a female big cat among her group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of lions, and the females form its core.

clue.text: Barren place was finally left to the antelope

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word left

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A dry wilderness was in the end abandoned to the grazing herds.
explanation.definitionFit: A desolate, infertile tract of land where nothing grows.

clue.text: Let one: Communist follow his lead

indicators.note: follow puts the following pieces after the letter taken from his
a word's lead is its opening letter, here from his

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
red is the traditional colour, and nickname, of a communist

explanation.surface: A party member is told to rent out a room, following the leader's example.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a house is to rent it out, so a let property has been taken on lease.

clue.text: Possess piece of furniture, charged up

parts.note: a bed is a piece of bedroom furniture

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for charged is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a live wire is electrically charged

explanation.surface: Someone wants to own a sofa bed bought on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for charged; 'Possess' is meant in the demonic sense, as an evil spirit possesses someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is said to possess or torment the person it haunts.

clue.text: Give permission for excess sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the entry is pronounced like the word for excess

parts.note: licence in British spelling can mean unrestrained excess, as in poetic licence

explanation.surface: A request for official approval to go overboard, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In British spelling the noun is LICENCE and the verb LICENSE; they are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise something formally, granting a permit.

clue.text: It might be better questioning "Does it matter?"

definitions.meaning: a better is someone who bets, who would ask about the price offered
an informal shrug meaning it makes no difference

explanation.surface: A philosophical shrug about whether improvement is worth asking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improved' but is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler asks the bookmaker's price; colloquially the phrase means who cares.

clue.text: Ghastly retreats, abandoning the last of the regiment

indicators.note: abandoning means a letter is dropped from the hiding places

parts.note: retreats are hiding places or hideaways

indicators.note: the last of points to the final letter of regiment

explanation.surface: Soldiers flee awful hideaways, leaving the last of their comrades behind.
explanation.walkthrough: HIDEOUTS loses the T that ends 'regiment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely ugly or horrible to look at.

clue.text: One of the grass-roots I'd clear out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician vows to purge a grass-roots activist from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass-roots' suggests local party members; it is literal roots of a grass plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The embryonic root of a seedling, the first part to emerge from a seed.

clue.text: Rebuild generally with his style of architecture

indicators.note: rebuild means the letters are taken apart and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A man generally restores buildings in his preferred architectural manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The first phase of English Gothic building, roughly the thirteenth century, with lancet windows.

clue.text: Test papers read out from the galley

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the entry sounds like the phrase for test papers

parts.note: try means test, and a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: Exam scripts are read aloud from the kitchen of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galley' suggests a ship's kitchen or a printer's proof; it is an ancient oared warship.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek warship rowed by three banks of oars.

clue.text: He'll find you some liquid more like nectar

definitions.meaning: a water dowser locates underground springs with a rod
comparative of divine, nectar being the drink of the gods

explanation.surface: A dowser who locates something tastier than water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser seeks water with a forked stick; also comparative of heavenly, as nectar is the gods' drink.

clue.text: By the sound of it, adjusts 23

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the entry is pronounced like the word for adjusts

parts.note: to true a wheel or frame is to adjust it into exact alignment

explanation.surface: A tailor alters clothing, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is APPAREL. TREWS are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan trousers are a garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Armament badly sited aboard vessel

indicators.note: sited aboard places the word for badly inside the vessel

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Guns are poorly positioned on a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Big guns and cannon collectively, a military weapon arm.

clue.text: End with a monstrous eyeless (so to speak) shrew

parts.note: a term is an end or limit, as in the end of a period

indicators.note: eyeless by sound means without the letter I, so it is dropped

parts.note: giant means monstrous, huge

explanation.surface: A nagging woman comes to a sticky end with a blinded monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyeless (so to speak)' removes I, said like 'eye', from GIANT, leaving GANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding, violent-tempered woman; shrew in its old sense of a nag.

clue.text: I'd be more original, having the right to add fanciful details

indicators.note: original suggests the letters are made new, rearranged into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A storyteller boasts of greater originality, entitled to dress up the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' simply joins: the rearranged letters are followed by the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish a story with invented touches, as needlework decorates cloth.

clue.text: Engineers abandon support for club

indicators.note: abandon means the letters for engineers are dropped from the support

parts.note: a brassiere is a supporting undergarment
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers stop sponsoring a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassie is an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wooden golf club with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: In general it provides protection

definitions.meaning: taken as a whole, on balance
a loose work garment worn over clothes to keep them clean

explanation.surface: A general remark on how something keeps you safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Means on the whole; also a protective work garment pulled on over clothes.

clue.text: In line — an ash

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A single tree standing in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Carpet salesman covers range

indicators.note: covers puts the salesman on top of the word for range in this down entry

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
to rove is to range or wander

explanation.surface: A rug seller travels across a wide area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is a verb here: to carpet someone is to give them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or rebuke formally, as a boss hauls a worker onto the carpet.

clue.text: Man with amazing powers to bring conflict to close

parts.note: war is armed conflict
to lock is to close fast

explanation.surface: A wizard has the power to end a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A male witch or sorcerer, one who practises magic.

clue.text: In despair, moving more than one square

indicators.note: moving shows the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in despair keeps moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural noun: nappies, squares of folded cloth in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies' nappies, traditionally folded squares of cloth.

clue.text: One's uplifted, with fresh strength

indicators.note: uplifted in a down entry means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: one is I, and 's gives S
new means fresh

explanation.surface: Someone cheered up has found renewed vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle power, a tendon being what gives a body force.

clue.text: A couple of pages are left in costume

parts.note: p is page, so two of them is pp

explanation.surface: Some pages of a costume book are left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing, dress, what one wears.

clue.text: Support us in a spot

indicators.note: in places the word us within the blemish

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: Back us when we are in a tight corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' suggests a predicament, but it is a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold or keep going, bearing the weight of.

clue.text: In love with alluring, not heartless girl

indicators.note: not means the letters that follow are taken away

parts.note: glamorous means alluring, attractive

indicators.note: heartless strips a word of its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Smitten with a charming girl who is far from cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAMOROUS loses GL, the first and last letters of 'girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing romantic or sexual desire, besotted.

clue.text: Wets O.K. really — it's unusual to see cowardice

indicators.note: unusual tells us the preceding letters form an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: Thinking bed-wetting is acceptable is an odd sign of timidity.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak of yellow in character means a lack of courage.
